about.title: Highland Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Highland residents rely daily on products ranging from household appliances to vehicle parts and tools used along corridors like SR-210 and 9th Street. When those products fail because of a design flaw, manufacturing error, or missing warning, the resulting injuries can be serious and unexpected. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused harm. That can make these cases move differently than a typical crash claim, especially with multiple companies in the supply chain who might share responsibility. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect Highland residents hurt by defective products with independent attorneys who understand how to evaluate manufacturing defects, design flaws, and failure-to-warn claims. If you've been injured by a product recently purchased or used in Highland, keeping the item itself and any packaging can matter, and speaking with an attorney early costs nothing through our free connection service.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Highland Claims

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, an injured person generally doesn't have to show the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the pool of parties an attorney can pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Is Key
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on physical evidence, keeping the defective product and its packaging intact can matter for a thorough review by an independent attorney.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the maker acted carelessly. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your specific case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or remaining pieces. This physical evidence often plays a central role in evaluating a product liability claim. Avoid repairing, discarding, or altering it before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: Is this only for products bought in Highland?
items.answer: No — what matters is where the injury happened, not necessarily where the product was purchased.
